- Target p95 generation latency: <= 200ms end-to-end (model inference only budget ~160ms)
- Expected traffic shape for week 1: avg 40 req/s, peak bursts up to 250 req/s for ~10 minute bursts during business hours
- Avg tokens per request: 420 (most chats include history), 95th tokens per request ~1024
- Model: open-weights Llama-2-13B (we plan to test both fp16 and int8 variants)

I've attached the workload CSV with sampled request timestamps and payload sizes. Can you provide a tokens/sec based sizing model and recommended GPU slab (A100/H100 equivalents) plus burst strategy? Also curious about the impact of prefix/KV caching and batching on our SLO.

Hi Alicia — thanks for the sample dataset, that was super helpful. We've run an initial tokens/sec analysis and sketched three sizing scenarios (conservative / expected / aggressive). Key assumptions up front:
- Average tokens per request (observed): 420; 95th = 980 (we used your CSV percentiles)
- Target inference budget: model-only p95 <= 160ms (we keep 40ms for network/queueing)
- Batching: we assume continuous batching with latency-aware cutoffs; effective batching factor varies with concurrency (we used an empirical batching curve)
- KV/prefix cache: expected hit rate 15% (history stabilization) — we include a scenario with 40% hit to show upside

Quick math (examples):
- If bursts reach 250 req/s and avg tokens = 420 => burst tokens/sec = 105,000 t/s.
- Measured tokens/sec per A100-equivalent for Llama-2-13B (int8 optimized, our runtime): ~7,000 t/s under 95ms p50 but p95 increases with variance. For H100-equivalent we measure ~12,000 t/s under similar quantization.
- Baseline GPU count (no cache, no batching gains): 105,000 / 7,000 ≈ 15 GPUs (A100-equivalent).
- With realistic batching and KV caching (15% hit + batching gains), effective tokens/sec per GPU increases ~25% => ~8,750 t/s => GPUs needed ≈ 12.

Headroom and SLO notes:
- For p95 <= 160ms we recommend adding 25% headroom above calculated bursts to account for traffic spikes and degraded quantization tails. That puts safe commit at ~15 A100-equivalent GPUs (12 * 1.25 ≈ 15).
- If you use H100 slab instead, recommended commit drops to ~8–10 GPUs with the same headroom.

Options to reduce commit:
1) Increase KV/prefix cache effectiveness (aim for 40% hit) — would reduce needed GPUs by ~30% at burst.
2) Use a smaller distilled model for non-critical requests and route via smart routing for cheap inference; keep full model for high-quality outputs.
3) Accept a higher p95 budget during rare extreme bursts and use bursting to cloud-hosted capacity.

Can we sync on two quick things so we can finalize a deliverable for procurement?
- Confirm target p95 at model-level (is 160ms firm?)
- Do you have a preference for GPU family (cost vs latency tradeoff) or should we produce both A100 and H100 costing?

I'll run a detailed slab/ops plan once I get those answers and include cost delta.

Cheers,
Marissa Cole
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Looping myself in with some ops-level color — a couple of practical constraints and suggestions:

- Autoscaling granularity: our Dedicated product supports per-customer slab with burstable headroom (burst to N extra GPUs for short windows). We typically recommend configuring burst windows with a 2‑minute cool-down to avoid flip-flopping.
- Pre-warm and warm-up: for chat-heavy workloads, KV cache warm-up can meaningfully reduce p95 for the first 10–30 minutes after a cold start. Suggest we include a warm-up plan for each daily peak.
- Prefetch/batched prompts: if Stratus can serve a small percentage of traffic as batched system prompts (e.g., analytics or templated replies), that increases batching efficiency without user-visible degradation.

Updated micro-benchmarks from infra (measured on our 2026 kernel):
- Llama-2-13B int8 on A100-equivalent: median 45ms per 512-token chunk; sustained throughput ≈ 7k t/s (as Marissa noted).
- H100-equivalent: median 28ms per 512-token chunk; sustained throughput ≈ 12.5k t/s.

Operational recommendation for the POC: commit to 16 A100-equivalent GPUs with a burst policy to +50% (24 GPUs) limited to 15 minutes/day for 30-day trial windows. That gives ~30% headroom above measured burst when caching/batching is imperfect. Cost illustration and fallback routes included in Marissa's workbook.

-ben

Hi Alicia — summarizing the recommended plan (slide deck & workbook attached):

1) Commit sizing (monthly reserved, POC slab):
   - Primary: 16 A100-equivalent GPUs (committed)
   - Burst: allow +50% burst (24 GPUs) for up to 15 minutes per day during business hours (automated policy)
2) SLO fit and headroom:
   - Expected model-level p95 with this configuration: ~150–170ms (measured on our stack, assumes 15% cache hits and conservative batching)
   - This leaves ~10–25ms buffer to stay under your 200ms end-to-end target once network/queueing is included.
3) Alternatives & cost tradeoffs:
   - Move to H100-equivalent slab => 9–10 GPUs committed, p95 improves to ~120–140ms, but unit cost increases ~1.8x.
   - Increase KV/prefix cache to 40% hit => reduces committed A100 count to ~11 GPUs (plus burst).
4) Execution checklist for procurement / ops:
   - Sign reserved commitment for STR-2027-014 (we'll issue contract variant with burst policy)
   - Schedule pre-provisioning week: run two warm-up passes to populate KV caches prior to go-live windows
   - Add health-check route & fallback: on OOM/overload route 20% of traffic to distilled model until backfill completes

Attachments: redwood_capacity_model_v2.xlsx (breakdown by slab, estimated monthly cost, sensitivity to cache hit rate) and the sample CSV you provided.

If that plan looks good I'll put together the formal procurement pack (cost sheet + SLA appendix + runbook) and loop in finance/contracts. Happy to hop on a 20-minute call tomorrow to walk procurement through the numbers.
